title: How wide is the NR band at 250 keV? Sensitivity of the '1.5 sigma below the median' statement to the yield break and fluctuation model
question: What sets sigma(log10 S2c) of the NR band at S1c ~ 540 phd, how does it depend on the NEST nr_er_width_parameters, the p(E) break, g1/g2, field and detector terms, how many AmBe events constrain it near 250 keV, what is P(log S2c <= observed | genuine 248 keV NR), and what fraction of the NR PDF lies inside the MSSI 68/95 % contours?
headline_result: The NR-band width at 540 phd is set by the binomial statistics of ~300 electrons (floor 0.023 dex): NEST gives 0.0313 dex and LZ's own AmBe points 0.036 +- 0.005 dex, so the paper's '1.5 sigma' (P ~ 6 %) is correct and the drawn 10-90 % lines (sigma_eq 0.0212, would give 2.3 sigma) are ~1.5x too narrow; the event is a typical NR-band member (4 of 31 AmBe points at 450-600 phd lie at or below its depth) and 81 %/100 % of the NR PDF sits inside the MSSI 68 %/95 % regions
key_numbers: sigma(540 phd) MC 0.0313 dex, median 4.015 (drawn 4.016); terms: recombination binomial 0.0231, extraction 0.0125, position 0.0087, SE Fano 0.0085, omega 0.0083, ion Fano 0.0062, slice mixing 0.0061; event 1.54 sigma, P(<=obs) 5.7 % (5.3 % at 248 keV); drawn half-width 0.0271+-0.0004 -> sigma 0.0212, 2.33 sigma, P 1.0 %; paper 1.5 sigma => sigma 0.0328; needs electron fluct. x0.41; width params +-30 %: <=3 % except W3 x0.7 -> 0.048, W4 x1.3 -> 0.038; W11=+0.3 -> 0.195; no break 5.0 sigma, NEST default 6.4 sigma; g2 +-3 % -> 1.10-1.99 sigma; pos 0/3/6 % -> 0.030/0.033/0.041; eps 0.726/1.0 -> 0.032/0.029; perfect detector 0.025, binomial floor 0.023; L10 contours => sigma >= 0.029; AmBe 19 pts 500-580 phd, 43 >450, none >600; isotropic model 1.2 % in 230-270 keV (~1800 events); sigma_median 0.007 dex, width +-16 %; residual sd 0.036+-0.005 (N=31), dlnL 11.4, 4/31 at/below event; MSSI edges at 540: 3.988 (68 %), 3.695 (95 %); NR PDF inside 81 %/100 %
model_or_mechanism: nestpy GetQuanta NR fluctuations (LZ_WS2024 width vector) + binomial S1/extraction, SE Fano, position residual; analytic variance decomposition; tick-calibrated digitisation of Fig. 2/4 NR lines and Fig. S1a MSSI/L10 contours; connected-component count and residual fit of Fig. 2 AmBe points; isotropic vs black-disk AmBe recoil spectrum bracket
stance: neutral (tool, projection, or constraint) - event is a typical NR-band member (strengthens NR compatibility vs P009's 2.5 sigma); band position cannot separate NR from MSSI
confidence: high for decomposition, floor and digitisation; medium for the AmBe-measured width (31 raster points incl. out-of-FV events) and the assumed extraction efficiency/position residual
